title: Sanskrit art integrated project
context: A Class X Sanskrit art integrated project at Delhi Public School, Jaipur, made with five classmates.
summary: This is a Class X group project on the state of Assam, written entirely in Sanskrit. It opens with a Sanskrit dialogue between two of us, Bhavya and me, about a trip to Assam, then covers the state's key facts, music, dance, food, arts and crafts, the Kamakhya temple and Kaziranga National Park.
points: Written entirely in Sanskrit, in Devanagari script, as a Class X art integrated project.
Sixteen slides on Assam: facts, music, dance, food, crafts, Kamakhya temple and Kaziranga.
A team of six students; framed as a Sanskrit conversation between Bhavya and Devansh.

body.p: The title slide reads **एकीकृत-कला-परियोजना-कार्यम् आसामाधारितम्** (an integrated art project based on Assam), for **कक्षा : दशमी** (Class X), **विषय : संस्कृत** (subject: Sanskrit), at दिल्ली पब्लिक स्कूल जयपुर.

Every slide is in Sanskrit. The project is framed as a conversation (भव्यादेवांशयोः मध्ये वार्तालापम्) in which Bhavya describes visiting the Kamakhya and Umananda temples and the Pobitora sanctuary, and I describe the Manas sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The other team members then take over different topics.

list: **Facts about Assam:** capital Dispur, area 78,438 sq km, state language Assamese, the Bihu festival, the Sattriya dance and the one-horned rhinoceros as state animal.
**Description:** an eastern state of India with 33 districts, set along the Brahmaputra and Barak rivers.
**Music and dance:** Bihu, Bodo, Karbi and Mising songs; instruments such as the pepa, toka, gogona, bahi, bin and doba; dances including Bihu, Bagurumba, Bhortal, Sattriya and Naga dance.
**Food:** rice, fish, mutton and chicken dishes, bamboo used for utensils and pickles, and tea, with Assam producing 50% of India's tea.
**Arts and crafts:** traditional craftspeople known for silk and bamboo work.
**Kamakhya temple:** one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, on Nilachal hill in western Guwahati, with the Ambubachi Mela as its annual festival.
**Kaziranga National Park:** spread across Golaghat, Karbi Anglong and Nagaon districts, a World Heritage Site known for the one-horned rhinoceros.
